newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM TO TAKE WORLD CUP SLALOM TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM TO TAKE WORLD CUP SLALOM TITLE.

text.p: Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden, after clinching the women's World Cup overall title with a third-place finish in the morning's super-g, added the exclamation point by winning the afternoon's slalom and season's slalom title Friday.
Wiberg, who had the second fastest time in the first leg of the slalom, produced a combined winning time of 1 minute, 17.90 seconds.
The victory also guaranteed Wiberg the slalom World Cup title for this season.

"It's amazing," Wiberg said after the two races. "My goal this season was to win the slalom cup. It was an extra surprise to also win the overall cup. I don't understand it yet, I think I need to sleep on it. Maybe in Vail when I actually get the cups, I will understand."

Just three tenths off Wiberg's pace in the second run was Sabine Egger of Austria. Egger had led the pack after the first run but her second-run time of 40.43 was not enough to take the win. She finished in second with a combined time of 1:18.15.
Taking third was Italy's Lara Magoni.
The course was a tight and technical slalom featuring 51 gates in the first run and 53 gates in the second run. Course conditions were firm and visibility was excellent.
